verdict.tagline: A brilliant literary detective story told entirely through text and dialogue.
for_you_if: you want a deep narrative experience like reading a rich book
you enjoy complex character builds shaping your investigation
you appreciate full voice acting and painterly art
not_for_you_if: you expect traditional action or combat systems
you dislike clunky movement or sudden game over states
you prefer fast-paced gameplay over extensive reading

distortion_flags.sentence: Review sentiment shifts positively as players spend more time progressing past initial mechanical frustrations and deep into the narrative.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as heavily dialogue-driven, resembling a book or interactive novel rather than a traditional game.

citations.review_text: Эта игра известна как книга, замаскированная под игру. Наверное, соглашусь. Кор геймплей здесь - чтение. Лучше проходить на оригинальном английском - язык в игре очень богатый и красивый. Если нет уверенности в своём английском - можно поставить родной язык вторым и по кнопке Q мгновенно видеть перевод. Я, хоть и неплохо знаю английский, пользуюсь - помгает расширить словарный запас
I mean if I want to read a book, i'll read a book.

This is one of the greatest games ever made. The writing, voice acting, and role-playability are on another level. It is a playable piece of art. The game is more of an interactive novel and the world and characters feel  very much alive. I would recommend this game to anyone and everyone; it won't be for everyone, but that's their loss.

It's more a book than a video game. Still amazing: great story, humor, and commentary on the real world. The first playthrough is magical, an experience where you are just like the protagonist: thrown into the world with no clue what's happening, piecing together parts of the case, the people (and forces) around you, and yourself. Sunrise, Parabellum. I wish Kim was real.
A game that people say is good, that actually is good. It's intriguing and really enjoyable for a game that is 99% reading. The story and characters are really well done.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that moving around the world feels clunky and slow, requiring repetitive clicking or walking speed adjustments.

citations.review_text: it doesnt autosave and you randomly die depending on the choices, dont even have to fail a check, no warning u dead. also you move to slowly so you have to spam click to move at a walking speed instead of crawing, should movbe like 5x faster

An interesting game but very flawed, do not get hyped by others to believe this is "the best rpg game ever"

Cons:
-Very clunky game, moving around feels awful and you have to do it ALOT
-"side-quests" are NOT optional, and must be done in the "good" way otherwise you can softlock yourself out of finishing the game. because you have to do 2 "impossible"(games own words) dialogue checks at a very specific point in the game. You can only "redo" this check if you level a specific skill, or save-scum alot. (you can only level so-many times, since there are leveling caps to skills)
-Multiple audio bugs, mostly around the music. It would constantly bug out seemingly when walking from one zone to another.
-Fast travel might aswell not be included, because you can only fast travel at very specific points and you have to be standing in these specific points aswell to initiate it. Fast travel for some reason do not advance ingame time, and just becomes teleporting. The way it is implemented is a joke.
-Character animations frequently last 10x longer than the voice from the voice actor (you cannot skip/advance, you HAVE to wait until the animation finishes) a good example is Titus, a character that has to slowly walk towards you every time you interact with him.
-Leveling skills feels useless, the thought cabinet or whatever was the only tangible "upgrade" to your character as frequently it felt like getting +1 or more to a skill barely moved the needle on checks, and was more intended to just retry failed checks. (with maybe a 3% boost from the new level)
-The thought cabinet was interesting, but you don't know what buff/debuff you will get from investing alot of ingame time from finishing ANY of these. it was so frustrating that i had to use an online wiki to just see if i was gonna waste my time on the thought cabinet.
-Censoring: why is there no option to turn this off? hearing a screeching sound every time someone swears (happens alot) is jarring, compared to ju…

cohorts.summary: Mid-tier players praise the extensive reading, full voice acting, and atmospheric art style, despite occasional frustrations with soft-locks and skill checks.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game features extensive reading and dialogue-heavy, text-driven gameplay with no combat system.

citations.review_text: DAMN YOU WILL READ A LOT OF TEXT AND DIALOGS!!!

It's the best written game I've ever played. It's also incredibly funny and engrossing gameplay-wise despite having no combat system. I'm meandering through it but can already tell it's a masterpiece. 

Plus, it looks like a painting on an OLED at 21:9, runs great on my steam deck and easily synch saves. All of these features are really nice and don't require me to tinker.

HAAAAAAARDCORE!

How can I explain this game? Perhaps it's impossible to describe. Art normally is. Whatever makes this game truly magnificent - and it is - I cant do it justice in a review. You just have to experience it. It's not a huge experience. It's something subtle. But it IS profound. It makes every other game feel flat in comparison.

The game is both boring and all consuming. Insanely deep and also remarkably linear. Characters which feel cliché but also nuanced and real. Studio ZA/UM have managed the impossible - to create the illusion that choice matters in a satisfying and meaningful way. I would recommend this game to you, wholeheartedly. Its in no way a game for everyone. But if you like point and click adventures, and have the patience to read a lot, there is something about this game that I have never found anywhere else.

One of the best storylines I've ever consumed in a video game, honestly maybe media in general. Its format as a videogame was probably the best formats to deliver its story in, anything else wouldn't have done it justice. The characters are almost all fascinating, and its almost impossible to not be pulled in.
 
Excellent art style, incredible and fascinating worldbuilding with hints of paranormality, excellent tone and pacing 
 
Overall a fantastic piece of media, a solid A+ in my book
 
The only less than stellar thing I can think to say about this game is that it doesn't have a lot of *gameplay* but thats not really what you're here for. Exploration and dialogue are the stars of the show here, and it pulls both of those off wonderfully. Some of the best I've ever had, more people need to experience this game.

I started this in a long list of steam backlog and I was instantly enamored with the story telling and art style. If you don't like reading this may not be a game for you. There is no combat but there is amazing voice acting, beautiful art, and an engaging story to keep the player interested until the end.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game includes full voice acting which enhances the emotional delivery of the narrative.

citations.review_text:
'Prepare to die from looking at a window and sitting on an uncomfortable chair for too long'. 
This game has been hailed by many as a "Must Play Essential", and I must conclude that it is genuinely spectacular. 

I played this game firstly on Hardcore, and while it took me a while to find my stride initially, as it was my first isometric RPG game of this style, taking my time to really understand the mechanics and really considering my narrative choices elucidated how purposeful and narratively rich this game is. The art style and score are just fantastic. Being berated by your internal psyche when you fail a skill check, or the quite frankly ridiculously hilarious impossible skill checks that can be completed, is what gives this game such a unique experience that has yet to be replicated in any other game I have played (as of yet). Your decisions genuinely and quite frequently make massive narrative changes making it impossible to fully experience everything in one or two playthroughs (unlike some games *cough* *cough* Telltale).  

Special commendations must go to the sublime voice acting in this game, with my particular favourites being Kim, Measurehead, and the Narrator voiced by Lenval Brown. His performance reminded me a lot of Kevin Michael Richardson, the voice of Zima Blue in "Love, Death and Robots", which is a massive compliment from me. 

My only qualm with the game was that there weren't preset outfit saves to maximise your attributes depending on what the narrative required. Some people may disagree, but during my first playthrough I really wanted to respect the mechanics. However, passing the skill checks overall yielded greater story exploration and experience, in my opinion, so I often found myself in the latter half of the game tweaking my outfit to increase my chances of passing. Another issue was that progression occasionally overlapped between side quests and the main quest, and prompts where you were exploring solo without Kim started including…

Disco Elysium - The Final Cut is one of the most unique RPGs ever made. The writing is on another level: sharp, funny, tragic, and endlessly clever. Talking to your own skills, failing spectacularly, and roleplaying a complete disaster of a detective feels incredible. The world of Revachol is rich, the characters stick with you, and the Final Cut’s full voice acting elevates everything.
It’s also extremely text heavy, slow paced, and can feel punishing early on when skill checks keep failing. The political themes are front and center, which some people love and others find exhausting. This is more of an interactive novel with RPG systems than a traditional game.

Unparalleled in writing, world building and tone, with gameplay that lets these strengths shine.

There are very few games that achieve good, surface level writing, let alone writing a world and story that feels fully real and authentic, and none do it like this game.

Every character, every building, every description of every item, every word, spoken or otherwise feels like it belongs in this alternate world, and works to let you immerse yourself in this world, marinating in its atmosphere and tone.

It can’t be overstated and I’m struggling to put it into words, this game has the best writing in any game. It comes with the type of game it is, a visual novel type RPG, and this game pushes this genre to its literary limits.

It is deep, depressing and highly cerebral, whilst also being incredibly funny, absurd, and sad.

The addition of voice acting post-launch would in any other game simply be there for flavour and be for the people who couldn’t be bothered to read, but in this game it adds another layer of emotion to the words being said. The pauses, the small inflections in their voice, the intensities and subtleties. It all makes these characters, these people, feel real.

There will be no game like this ever again, it truly is one of a kind.

I started this in a long list of steam backlog and I was instantly enamored with the story telling and art style. If you don't like reading this may not be a game for you. There is no combat but there is amazing voice acting, beautiful art, and an engaging story to keep the player interested until the end.

citations.review_text:
Such an incredible piece of art! i haven't made it far into the game only having proceeded to day 2 as of writing this "review". But! This game is incredible! The art, dialoge, psychological depth, music, and overall atmosphere are top tier. It's so beautifully illustrated with a impressionistic feel together with the soft seashore jazzy tone. The music contrasts the atmosphere so well with and also pairs perfectly with the murder mystery trope!

I had sort of lost interest in gaming during the last year or so until playing this. having replaced gaming with a cultural strive for literacy and academic approval through reading and writing. But thats also precisely the reason for why i hold this game in such high regard compared to most other games! It satisfies every philomatical desire of mine that Hesse, Girard, Jung, Nietzsche and so many others have done for the past few months. As well as also succeeding in producing a really interactive gaming experience! 

Harry Du Bous is definitely one of the most intriguing pathways into identity's complexion and modern individuality's proportion to society. He funnily enough reminds me of Harry Haller and the whole jungian idea of self through layers of collective archetypes within the human psyche.

I also think the game has hilarious characters and dynamics that work amazingly towards developing a fantastic insight into one of the hardest subjects to depict fairly within art. Thoughts. This game depicts human thinking in a incredibly creative and fun manner that gives room for reevaluation within your thinking no matter who you are. And that can be philosophical thinking within basically every field imaginable, politics, marxism, capitalism, existentialism, psychology, self, regret, etc... 

A game with all this BRILLIANT political and psychological commentary is a groundbreaking experience together with the INCREDIBLE art and music! It's most definitely a must play for whoever managed to stand out with reading th…

I'm surprising no one when I say Disco Elysium is fantastic, its not really all that surprising to hear it's an instant classic and immediately one of my favorite games of all time. This game, a game that by all accounts of trends, social considerations and “common business wisdom” managed to be a runaway success only diminished by the real world drama of its publisher screwing over its leads. Still, no one can diminish its achievement when we live in a world with Disco Elysium-likes.

So what makes it special? So much. Mechanically its unique presentation and systems basically exploding the obsidian concept of skills as dialogue tools and making them active parts of narration, and thematically tied to the concept of a fractured self. Presentationally, in its strikingly stylistic art style pulling from abstract and cubist art styles, its sharp comedy and confident criticism of our world. Music that while not particularly calling attention to itself is coated in nostalgia and an ache that makes you want to sit down watch the sea and feel the weight of reality. Wrap that all with a compelling set of mysteries it's hard not to adore.

I say mysteries as not only is the core murder your solving compelling, almost every side quest spirals out from a starting idea into an incredible web of interconnected subquests. One minute you're looking for a freezer to store a body which leads to investigating a cursed business district, all of which ends up important hours later when you're working with some homeless teens and programming uncovering a hole in the universe tucked into a church. Each step being genuinely interconnected and compelling all on its own.

Still more than that I think for me the thing that truly propels Disco Elysium, more than the mystery, or the comedy, than the absolutely cutting political comedy, is the artistic honesty. While its built in self critic that feels utterly honest, one can tell the creative directors history of alcoholism is a key ins…

PERCEPTION (SIGHT) [Difficulty: Heroic — Success]
CHECK: [Perception (Sight)]
BASE CHANCE: 17% (2d6 + 3 Motorics + 2 "Art Cop" Thought)
DICE ROLL: [6, 5] + 5 = 16 — SUCCESS
You see a masterpiece encrusted with salt, diesel oil, and rust. Martinaise isn't a place, Branc: it is a monumental carcass stranded on the precipice of history.

Thick, furious oil brushstrokes—applied as if the painter had dragged their own knuckles through the sludge and ash of a long-dead revolution. The palette reeks of industrial lead, winter sea, and stagnant flesh, pierced only by the violent twitch of a neon sign bleeding into the sea-mist. Every corner is a historical layer of trauma: bullet holes on the brick facades are forty years old, yet they still appear open, wet, and oozing.

This is not mere art direction; it is the visual anatomy of failure. An impressionist canvas where even the snow falls heavy and grey, utterly incapable of bleaching away Martinaise's sins.

Talking to your own skills, failing spectacularly, and roleplaying a complete disaster of a detective feels incredible. The world of Revachol is rich, the characters stick with you, and the Final Cut’s full voice acting elevates everything.
It’s also extremely text heavy, slow paced, and can feel punishing early on when skill checks keep failing. The political themes are front and center, which some people love and others find exhausting. This is more of an interactive novel with RPG systems than a traditional game.

At first, the game really grabbed me with its unique presentation - it was the first detective game I’d ever played (I think). I liked the storytelling, the interesting characters, and the interaction with the world. But there’s one major drawback that overshadows all the positives - the game’s plot progression is simply awful. You can get stuck in a soft lock and end up wandering the map for hours, trying to figure out where to go, who to talk to, and what to do. And this waste of time feels like a mockery. On top of that, there’s already way too much text in the game, which forces you to stay in one place for long stretches. Overall, I’d give it a 4/10.

claims.claim: Reviewers advise against supporting the publisher due to business actions taken against the original developers.

citations.review_text: one of the best games i've ever played, i have nothing bad to say about it. however, please pirate it. the actual devs are getting no money from this bc the publishers essentially just stole it from them. all things aside, the art's beautiful, the music's amazing, and i wish i could forget the game just to play it again for the first time.

One of the best piece of fictional literature ever made, ranging from interactions, musics, message, artwork, and world building, easy 10/10 from me.
The peak embodiment of "game is an art form".

Also, fuck za/um for laying off the OG devs.

Imagine a group of talented, passionate people came together, started a movement and dreamed up a an exciting new reality for themselves at first, and then shared it with the world. Of course, behind the scenes things were fraught and far from perfect but the blood, sweat and tears of decades culminated in something truly unique, revolutionary (of sorts) and moved the masses. Old ideas made new in something totally unique, something totally and unashamedly itself.

That is, until the forces of capital reared its ugly head and let slip the mask of humanity to crush whatever creative new force that had arisen. Claiming the scalps of those who had birthed this new idea to totally subsume and exploit whatever ruins were left.

I wish what I just described were solely events that happened in the historical lore of the game, but sadly it has crossed the boundary of the pale into reality. What started out as a passion project by a collective of Estonian artists and writers has been hijacked by white collar criminals. The original creative team was fired and most of the company laid off by the majority shareholders of ZA/UM who used loopholes and financial manipulation to gain control of the golden goose.

Pirate this game, because this is a narrative experience like no other. (I bought this years ago before all the news broke out about the criminality of the current management) A truly brilliant Post-Soviet work of art that could have never been made by any other people at any other time. 10/10.

One day I will return to your side.

I love this game a lot and it's one of the greatest of all time, but the studio has kicked out all of its devs to reap the cash in their stead so I cannot recommend it ON STEAM. elsewhere may be okay but don't give money to a studio that bleeds the very hearts of their game dry.
Wonderful game legit one of my favorites. But screw the publishers, stole everything from the people who actually made the game.

claims.claim: This cohort describes the game as text-heavy, resembling reading a book or listening to an audiobook.

citations.review_text:
Great game great story great characters, amazing twists and politics. Amazing world building and lore, and decisions matter and people die, lie betray, are paranoid and eccentric.
Gameplay is obviously lacking and really sticks out like a sore thumb when you try to do all the side-quests.
The ending is very satisfying and everything gets resolved at the end, at least it did in my play through.

Get game but be ready to sit though hours of dialog, essentially a playable audio book but its great.

At the moment of writing this review, I made the second playthrough and planning to do the third one after the break. Despite not having a huge map, this game has a lot of content to explore. Characters which can be met throughout the story are diverse and you will definitely have many interesting conversations with them. Expect a lot of reading/listening. The majority of the game feels like an audiobook, but that's one of the aspects for which I liked it actually).

Although, I would like to add a bit of realism. I am not sure if it is because of my Mac (99% it runs pretty smoothly on it actually), but occasionally the game just randomly froze and I was forced to restart. It didn't make me to write a completely negative review, but it is worth to note. Personally, I just recommend to save more often.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game includes no combat, featuring instead a detective investigation driven by dialogue and skill checks.

citations.review_text:
I bought a detective game and spent the first ten minutes looking for my own shoes. [spoiler]Meanwhile there is a man who's been hanging behind the hostel for a week and nobodys bothered, which says a lot about the neighbourhood[/spoiler]

No fighting. You talk, roll dice and fail. Your own skills chat to you constantly and half of them are idiots. You have got health and morale, so you can die from a conversation. Nearly like Christmas.

The detective work is brilliant. [spoiler]Getting the body down is a job in itself[/spoiler], then everyone lies to your face, especially some dockworkers who clearly did [i]something[/i]. Kim writes it all down and pretends you're competent. Give that man a pay rise!

Played it as a genius, an idiot and a communist. Got every achievement and kept going.

[spoiler]I cried at a stick insect.[/spoiler]

[strike]A good game[/strike] PERFECT GAME

Disco Elysium may be both the single best detective game and single best CRPG to ever be made.  And all that without combat.  

Not only does it possibly have the best and most iconic writing in all of videogaming, the world building is phenomenally deep and, thanks to being a CRPG at its core, you can easily do multiple playthroughs to approach the quests in a multitude of different ways.

It's also a killer app for language learners such as myself, as it allows you to toggle between two languages with the press of a button.  Other devs, please take note.

And as a bonus, it's pretty much the perfect Steam Deck game.

S+ tier without a question.  You should probably play this.

[strike]A good game[/strike] PERFECT GAME

If you're looking for an action game, turn around. Disco Elysium is basically a tabletop RPG where your biggest enemy is your own apocalyptic hangover. You play as a detective whose brain is so fried he forgot his own name, and instead of a standard skill tree, you level up 24 different voices in your head that constantly argue with each other.

Min-max your physical stats and you can roundhouse kick a racist; min-max your psyche and your hideous necktie starts giving you supernatural career advice. You can literally fail an RNG dice roll and die from sitting in an uncomfortable chair or trying to grab your shoe off a ceiling fan. The Final Cut adds incredible voice acting to this absolute chaos so you don't have to read a novel in silence. If you want an unhinged disaster of a human being, here is your game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game runs well on Linux and Steam Deck hardware.

citations.review_text:
As a fan of games where an exciting story and meaningful choices matter more than fast clicking I was expecting too much from the overrated game.
Disco Elysium is a very linear RPG with over complicated skills set.
Nearly 80% of those who started  this game never completed it despite wrote a positive review (don't trust in reviews of people who played less than 16h - you can not complete this game that fast), it starts well but quickly becomes a circle clicking and back and forth running, that's where they all give up forgetting to update the review.

pros:
atmosphere (in the first part of the game)
music
art
voice acting 
runs on linux without any issues

cons:
a very naive story trying to mimic Strugatski brothers and Émile Zola 
over complicated skill system 
easy to lock yourself 
reload awarding play-through
time consuming (you need to change clothes on every interaction with an NPC)
some quests are absolutely idiotic and will require you walk through same dialog tree 5 + times or run around (very boring and time consuming)
promotes usage of alcohol and other substances

TLDR: Get yourself an actual art degree and play this game. 

After 60 hours, I rolled the credits on Disco Elysium with a "good cop" run where my detective got his act together. Sort of.  With level of psychic trauma many of these characters have it’s doubtful anyone really has a truly happy ending. The preceding 40 hours went into three earlier attempts that I restarted because I wasn't happy with my character’s progression. The game encourages you to roll with the punches instead of save scumming, but by the end of in game day 2 I was so invested in the characters that I wanted the protagonist to get a favorable resolution. 

The writing for this game is on another level. It explores the human condition with a depth and level of empathy you rarely see in games, and it's worth playing for the narrative alone. It’s a shame what happened with Za/um’s writing team, as we will likely not get a video game story of this quality for the foreseeable future. 

It also runs great on the Steam Deck. I played on medium to high settings with no tweaks and got average battery life. The fan only kicked in during dialog-heavy segments. 

The gameplay has classic CRPG bones but is streamlined, since you only manage one character's skills and gear.

Finally, the subtle score by Sea Power is an understated masterpiece in-and-of itself, punctuating heavy moments and never over staying its welcome. Highly recommended if you play video games for narrative experiences.

citation.review_text:
If you're looking for an action game, turn around. Disco Elysium is basically a tabletop RPG where your biggest enemy is your own apocalyptic hangover. You play as a detective whose brain is so fried he forgot his own name, and instead of a standard skill tree, you level up 24 different voices in your head that constantly argue with each other.

Min-max your physical stats and you can roundhouse kick a racist; min-max your psyche and your hideous necktie starts giving you supernatural career advice. You can literally fail an RNG dice roll and die from sitting in an uncomfortable chair or trying to grab your shoe off a ceiling fan. The Final Cut adds incredible voice acting to this absolute chaos so you don't have to read a novel in silence. If you want an unhinged disaster of a human being, here is your game.
